name: Yeh'kinya
summary: At Steamwheedle Port, Yeh'kinya sends travelers in search of lost troll relics. The jungle troll scholar says he seeks ancient lore and artifacts to understand dark powers.

sections.title: The Scholar at Steamwheedle Port
sections.body: Among Steamwheedle Port's goblins and dockworkers, Yeh'kinya studies history and spirits. He sends travelers across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms in search of rare magical items. Some are ancient eggs in the Hinterlands. Others are stone prophecy tablets buried in Zul'Farrak. Yeh'kinya says this work serves the peaceful study of ancient troll history, though his focus on the blood god Hakkar draws suspicion.

sections.title: The Serpent's Deceit
sections.body: Yeh'kinya worships Hakkar the Soulflayer beneath his scholar's guise. He gathers artifacts and soul essence to prepare the Blood God's physical rebirth in Azeroth. Prospector Ironboot pieces together the plot and exposes it. Then Yeh'kinya abandons any pretense of friendship. He transforms into a green wind serpent and flees south across the open sea. The duped heroes must seek aid from the Zandalari on Yojamba Isle.

faq.answer: At Steamwheedle Port in Tanaris, Yeh'kinya is a jungle troll who stands near the water. He presents himself as a scholar of historical relics and spirits, with particular interest in the troll god Hakkar.

faq.q: Why does Yeh'kinya want the Prophecy of Mosh'aru and the Ancient Egg?
faq.answer: Yeh'kinya says the Prophecy of Mosh'aru and the Ancient Egg aid his study of ancient troll history and spirits. The tablets lie in Zul'Farrak's ruins, and the egg is in the Hinterlands. Both connect to his interest in Hakkar.

angles.text: As a Darkspear troll, you recognize the mortal peril of Hakkar's return.
As a priest, you may find Yeh'kinya's casual gathering of trapped screecher spirits troubling if you are sensitive to spiritual essence.
